Independent research directory · Begun October 19, 2026 · Updated October 26, 2026 · Entries include peoples, nations, communities, historical terms, and overlapping names. Entry counts are not a count of distinct nations. Source guides are starting points for further research. Saved entries stay in this browser.

  • Atlas brand collage

    Brand collage supplied by the Atlas owner

  • Interactive region map

    Outlines & lakes: Natural Earth · public domain. Generalized 1:50 million navigation map; lake shorelines are displayed separately from administrative boundaries.

  • Indigenous American Nations map

    Map: Peter Klumpenhower (Diné), Indigenous American Nations, c.16th Century, second edition (2024). The creator dedicates the map and its geometry to the public domain; the Atlas provides this courtesy credit and does not imply the creator’s endorsement. Open the full-resolution image ↗ · Creator’s edition notes · Original download and reuse terms · CC0 1.0.

  • Historical-map room background

    Background: Catawba map, copied manuscript after an Indigenous draught; maker unnamed. Supplied reproduction, exact scan provenance unconfirmed. LOC historical record · Dates, credit & reuse.

  • Smithsonian language-map invitation

    El Osario, Chichén Itzá · Photo: Álvaro de la Paz Franco
    Photo source · CC0 1.0 · Display notes

  • Directory landscape

    Backdrop: Canyon de Chelly · Navajo Nation · Photo: Margie Roesch · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Photo source & credit

  • Reading-room background

    Background: Manatvs, Joan Vinckeboons (Vingboons), surviving copy after a 1639 map. Library of Congress, Geography and Map Division · Dates, credit & reuse.

  • Acoma Pueblo artwork in the map sidebar

    Acoma Pueblo artist, name unrecorded. Water Jar, about 1880. The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Museum Accession, X.2.418. Artwork & image source · Public Domain / Met Open Access (CC0) · Image display record. The source photograph is unchanged; the layout applies cropping and a translucent overlay.

  • Apache basketry link decoration

    Apache artist, name unrecorded. Storage basket, ca.1890. The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Diker Collection; gift of Charles and Valerie Diker,2019. Object and photograph source · Public Domain / CC0 · Display record. Two CSS detail crops of the existing photograph; specific Apache nation unidentified.

  • Homepage entry-link patterns

    Original AI-assisted vector decoration: ocean waves and leaves, ice facets, and interlacing ribbons, created for the owner’s requested Hawaiian, Inuit and Cherokee themes. Contemporary design, not reproductions of traditional art or historical evidence.

  • Shared decorative illustration

    AI-generated background artwork, created at the Atlas owner’s request. Context & generation record.
